name: Cboe Global Markets
desc: Operator of US and European exchanges for options, equities, futures and FX, including the VIX volatility index franchise.
markets: Exchanges in the US, Canada, Europe and Australia; serves brokers and institutional traders worldwide.
rationale: Exchange brands such as Nasdaq already partner F1; B2B hospitality with trading firms and global market-data visibility.

name: Alight
desc: Provider of cloud-based employee benefits, health and retirement administration services for large employers.
markets: Mainly large US employers, with some international clients; no verified expansion plans beyond current footprint.
rationale: B2B hospitality for HR and benefits buyers at large employers; US-centric business limits global F1 value.
changed: Sold its payroll and professional services business to H.I.G. Capital in 2024

name: Egis
desc: French engineering and consulting group designing and operating transport, water and building infrastructure, plus airport and road concessions.
markets: Projects in over 100 countries across Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific and the Americas.
rationale: B2B hospitality with governments and infrastructure clients in Gulf and Asian race markets; limited consumer brand need.
changed: Tikehau Capital acquired a 40% stake from Caisse des Depots in 2022

name: China International Marine Containers (CIMC)
desc: Chinese manufacturer of shipping containers, road transport vehicles, energy equipment and airport ground-handling equipment.
markets: Sells to shipping lines, logistics and energy companies worldwide, with plants in China, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Industrial B2B maker with no consumer brand; hospitality value for logistics clients is the only angle.

name: Assurant
desc: Specialty insurer providing device protection, extended warranties, vehicle service contracts and renters and lender-placed housing insurance.
markets: Operates in North America, Latin America, Europe and Asia-Pacific through carrier, retail and auto partners.
rationale: B2B2C insurer with carrier and automotive partners; hospitality and auto tie-in plausible but brand rarely marketed directly.

name: Infosys
desc: Indian IT services company providing consulting, digital transformation, cloud, outsourcing and Finacle banking software to large enterprises.
markets: Clients mainly in North America and Europe, plus India and Asia-Pacific; delivery centres worldwide.
rationale: Rival IT services firms sponsor F1; technology showcase and B2B hospitality with global enterprise clients.

name: GEMS Education
desc: Operator of private kindergarten, primary and secondary schools offering international curricula, mainly in the Middle East.
markets: Schools mainly in the UAE and wider Middle East, with some schools in Asia, Europe and North America.
rationale: Strong Gulf presence aligns with Abu Dhabi and Middle East races; affluent expatriate parent audience.

name: Inspired Education Group
desc: Operator of premium private schools from kindergarten to secondary level, plus online schooling, across many countries.
markets: Over 100 schools across Europe, Africa, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific and the Americas.
rationale: Affluent family audience across many race markets; F1 fit is plausible but not an obvious category.

name: Eruditus
desc: Executive education company offering online and blended university programmes for professionals under the Emeritus brand.
markets: Learners and corporate clients in India, Asia, North America, Europe and Latin America.
rationale: Professional learner audience overlaps F1 fans; plausible for brand awareness but limited marketing budgets.

name: Sodexo
desc: Food services and facilities management company providing catering and on-site services to corporate, education, healthcare and sports venues.
markets: Operates in about 43 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Middle East.
rationale: Sports and event hospitality operator; F1 venue catering and corporate hospitality offer a direct commercial fit.
changed: Spun off its Pluxee employee benefits business in 2024

name: News Corp
desc: Media and information company owning Dow Jones, HarperCollins, News UK, News Corp Australia and digital real estate businesses.
markets: Operations in the US, UK and Australia, with publishing and information customers worldwide.
rationale: Media partnerships with F1 exist; WSJ, Times and Australian titles reach affluent audiences in race markets.
changed: Sold Foxtel to DAZN in 2025

name: Grupo Cibest (Bancolombia)
desc: Colombian financial group offering retail, corporate and investment banking, insurance and the Nequi digital wallet.
markets: Customers in Colombia, Panama, El Salvador, Guatemala and Puerto Rico; no verified wider expansion plans.
rationale: Large Latin American consumer bank; F1 has Latin American fans but Colombia has no race, so fit is moderate.
changed: Grupo Cibest holding company created over Bancolombia in 2025

name: Duolingo
desc: Maker of a gamified language-learning app, with maths, music and chess courses and the Duolingo English Test.
markets: Users worldwide across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Consumer brand with viral marketing and global young audience; fits F1 social-media and fan engagement.

name: Kobalt
desc: Music publishing and rights administration company collecting royalties for songwriters and independent publishers.
markets: Offices in the US, UK, Europe and Asia-Pacific serving songwriters worldwide.
rationale: Music-industry B2B business with little consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond possible content tie-ins.
changed: Sold its AWAL recordings business to Sony Music in 2022

name: Akamai Technologies
desc: Provider of content delivery network, cybersecurity and cloud computing services to enterprises and online businesses.
markets: Enterprise customers worldwide across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Cybersecurity and cloud rivals sponsor F1; technology showcase for streaming and data delivery.
changed: Acquired Linode in 2022

name: Live Nation Entertainment
desc: Live entertainment company promoting concerts, operating venues and festivals, and selling tickets through Ticketmaster.
markets: Concerts and ticketing in over 40 countries across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Live-events expertise and sponsorship sales fit Grand Prix entertainment and ticketing partnerships.

name: ADP
desc: Provider of payroll, human resources, benefits and workforce management software and outsourcing to businesses.
markets: Serves businesses across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Long motorsport sponsorship history in NASCAR and IndyCar; B2B hospitality and global brand reach.

name: Fosun International
desc: Chinese conglomerate with businesses in health, insurance, asset management, tourism such as Club Med, and property.
markets: Operations in over 35 countries across Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Owns Club Med and Wolves; leisure and consumer brands could use F1, but the group is deleveraging.

name: Magic Leap
desc: Developer of augmented reality headsets and optics technology for enterprise, healthcare and defence customers.
markets: Enterprise customers mainly in the US and Europe, plus optics partnerships with technology companies.
rationale: AR technology showcase for fan and engineering use, but small enterprise sales limit budget.

name: Mediobanca
desc: Italian banking group offering corporate and investment banking, wealth management and Compass consumer credit.
markets: Mainly Italy, with offices in Frankfurt, London, Madrid, Luxembourg, New York and Paris.
rationale: Italian finance brand with wealth clients; Monza hospitality plausible but now controlled by MPS.
parent: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena
changed: Monte dei Paschi di Siena acquired majority control in 2025

name: Strabag
desc: Construction group delivering building, civil engineering and transport infrastructure projects and property services.
markets: Home markets Austria and Germany, Central and Eastern Europe, plus Middle East, Canada, Chile and Australia.
rationale: B2B contractor with little need for global consumer branding; Austrian GP hospitality the main angle.

name: Accenture
desc: Professional services company providing consulting, technology, operations and AI services to corporations and governments.
markets: Clients in more than 120 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Consulting rivals such as Deloitte and PwC sponsor F1; technology showcase and executive hospitality.

name: Norsk Hydro
desc: Aluminium and renewable energy company producing primary aluminium, extrusions, recycled metal and hydropower.
markets: Operations in about 50 countries; customers in automotive, building and packaging worldwide.
rationale: Low-carbon aluminium supplier to car makers; sustainability tie-in plausible but B2B commodity profile.
changed: Acquired Sapa in 2017

name: Marvell Technology
desc: Fabless semiconductor company designing custom AI accelerators, optical, networking and storage chips for data centres.
markets: Customers are cloud providers and equipment makers in North America, Asia-Pacific and Europe.
rationale: Chip rivals such as AMD and Qualcomm sponsor F1; technology showcase for AI infrastructure.
changed: Sold its automotive Ethernet business to Infineon in 2025

name: Cenovus Energy
desc: Integrated oil and gas company producing oil sands crude and operating refineries and Canadian fuel retail.
markets: Operations in Canada and the US, plus offshore assets in Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Oil majors sponsor F1, but Cenovus sells mainly in North America; Canadian GP the main angle.
changed: Acquired Husky Energy in 2021 and MEG Energy in 2025

name: Lightspeed Commerce
desc: Provider of cloud point-of-sale, payments and e-commerce software for retailers, restaurants and golf courses.
markets: Customers in over 100 countries, mainly North America, Europe and Australia.
rationale: Hospitality and retail POS supplier; B2B fit at Grand Prix venues but marketing budgets limited.

name: IM8
desc: Nutritional supplement brand co-founded with David Beckham, selling daily nutrition drink mixes direct to consumers online.
markets: Sells mainly online to consumers in the US and other markets; exact country footprint not verified.
rationale: Celebrity-backed consumer health brand built on sport; F1 fan audience fits wellness and performance positioning.

name: Xylem
desc: Water technology company making pumps, meters, treatment equipment and analytics for utilities, industry and buildings.
markets: Operates in over 150 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and emerging markets.
rationale: Sustainability and water-efficiency story, with B2B hospitality for utility and industrial clients; not an obvious fit.
changed: Acquired Evoqua Water Technologies in 2023

name: Sonangol
desc: Angolan state oil company producing crude oil and gas with international partners and running refining and fuel distribution.
markets: Operations mainly in Angola, with crude sold to international buyers; restructuring ahead of planned partial privatisation.
rationale: State oil companies such as Aramco and Petronas sponsor F1, but Angola has no race and budgets are under reform.
changed: Concession and regulatory role moved to the ANPG agency in 2019 during restructuring

name: OpenAI
desc: Artificial intelligence company developing GPT models, the ChatGPT app, Codex and an API for developers and enterprises.
markets: Consumers, developers and enterprises worldwide across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: AI rivals such as Anthropic, Google and Meta partner F1 teams; strong technology showcase and consumer reach.
changed: Restructured as OpenAI Group PBC under the nonprofit OpenAI Foundation in 2025

name: Boldyn Networks
desc: Neutral host network company building and operating shared wireless, 5G, WiFi and fibre networks for transit systems, venues and cities.
markets: Networks in the UK, US, Canada, Australia and other European countries.
rationale: Venue and stadium connectivity provider; F1 circuit networks offer a technology showcase, though brand is B2B.
changed: Renamed from BAI Communications to Boldyn Networks in 2023

name: Franklin Resources (Franklin Templeton)
desc: Asset manager operating as Franklin Templeton, managing funds for retail investors, institutions and sovereign clients.
markets: Clients in over 150 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Asset managers such as Nuveen and Carlyle partner F1; global wealth audience and client hospitality.
changed: Acquired Legg Mason in 2020 and Putnam Investments in 2024

name: Oerlikon
desc: Swiss industrial group providing surface coatings and additive services for tools and parts, plus polymer processing equipment.
markets: Industrial customers in Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Americas, with sites in over 35 countries.
rationale: Coatings used in motorsport and automotive parts give a technology tie-in; limited consumer brand need.

name: Sandisk
desc: Maker of NAND flash memory, solid-state drives, memory cards and USB drives for consumers, devices and data centres.
markets: Sold worldwide through retailers and to device makers and data centres across all major regions.
rationale: Recognisable consumer storage brand; data and technology showcase fits F1 partner categories.
changed: Spun off from Western Digital in 2025

name: Box
desc: Cloud content management company offering secure file sharing, collaboration, e-signature and AI tools to enterprises.
markets: Enterprise and government customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Rivals Dropbox and others partner F1 teams; B2B software showcase and enterprise hospitality.

name: Lazard
desc: Financial advisory and asset management firm advising on mergers, restructuring and capital raising and managing client assets.
markets: Offices across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Elite advisory brand; B2B hospitality with corporate and sovereign clients plausible but little marketing culture.

name: Collinson Group
desc: Travel benefits and loyalty company running Priority Pass airport lounge access, travel insurance and loyalty programmes.
markets: Priority Pass lounges in over 150 countries; clients are banks, card issuers and airlines worldwide.
rationale: Affluent frequent-traveller audience mirrors F1 hospitality guests; strong fit for card and travel partners.

name: Xreal
desc: Maker of consumer augmented reality glasses that connect to phones, laptops and consoles to display virtual screens.
markets: Sold in China, Japan, South Korea, North America and Europe through retail and online.
rationale: Consumer tech brand targeting gamers and travellers; F1 viewing and gaming tie-ins plausible.
changed: Renamed from Nreal to Xreal in 2023

name: Johnson Controls
desc: Building technology company making HVAC, fire, security and building automation systems for commercial and public buildings.
industry: building HVAC, fire and security systems
markets: Operations across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Smart-building and energy-efficiency story; B2B hospitality for facility clients; stadium naming deals show sports interest.
changed: Sold its residential and light commercial HVAC business to Bosch in 2025

name: Kiteworks
desc: Cybersecurity company offering a private data network to protect sensitive email, file sharing and data exchange.
markets: Enterprise and government customers mainly in North America and Europe.
rationale: Cybersecurity is an active F1 category; small private vendor with limited budget for top-tier deals.
changed: Rebranded from Accellion to Kiteworks

name: Rockwell Automation
desc: Maker of industrial automation hardware and software, including Allen-Bradley controls, FactoryTalk software, drives and safety products.
markets: Customers in more than 100 countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Manufacturing technology showcase and B2B hospitality; history of motorsport sponsorship supports fit.

name: Persona
desc: Identity verification platform helping businesses verify users, prevent fraud and meet KYC and AML compliance requirements.
markets: Business customers mainly in the US, with some international clients; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Venture-backed B2B software with low brand awareness; F1 fit is weak beyond security-category activations.

name: Kyndryl
desc: IT infrastructure services provider running data centre, cloud, mainframe, network and security services for large enterprises.
markets: Customers in about 60 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: IT services rivals such as Cognizant and DXC sponsor F1; B2B hospitality and technology showcase.
changed: Spun off from IBM in 2021

name: Beko
desc: Home appliance brand selling washing machines, refrigerators, ovens and small appliances to households through retailers.
markets: Sold in more than 100 countries, mainly Europe, Turkey, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Consumer brand with football, basketball and tennis sponsorship history; strong European fan overlap.
changed: Beko Europe formed in 2024 by combining Arcelik and Whirlpool European operations

name: Pop Mart
desc: Designer and retailer of collectible toys and blind-box figures such as Labubu and Molly, sold through stores and online.
markets: Stores and online sales in China, South-East Asia, North America, Europe and Australia.
rationale: Fast-growing global consumer brand popular with young fans; F1 collectibles and fan engagement potential.

name: GitLab
desc: DevSecOps software platform covering source code management, CI/CD, security scanning and deployment for software teams.
markets: Customers worldwide across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; remote-first workforce.
rationale: Developer software rivals such as Atlassian and Vercel partner F1; technology showcase and enterprise hospitality.

name: VinFast Vietnam JSC
desc: Vietnamese operating company of VinFast, manufacturing electric cars and e-scooters at its factory in Hai Phong.
markets: Sells in Vietnam, the US, Canada, Europe and other Asian markets; expanding with plants in India and Indonesia.
rationale: Car makers use F1 for brand building; VinFast markets heavily and seeks international awareness.

name: Church & Dwight
desc: Consumer products maker of Arm & Hammer, OxiClean, Trojan, Batiste, Waterpik and Hero acne patches, sold through retailers.
markets: Mainly North America, with international sales in Europe, Australia, Latin America and Asia.
rationale: Household brands sell mostly in North America; individual brands could use US races, but fit is limited.

name: Campari Group
desc: Spirits group producing Campari, Aperol, Wild Turkey, Grand Marnier, SKYY, Espolon and Appleton Estate brands.
markets: Sells in more than 190 countries, with key markets in the US, Italy, Europe and Australia.
rationale: Spirits brands such as Heineken and Moet use F1; Aperol and Campari have strong event marketing.

name: HCLTech
desc: Indian IT services company providing software engineering, cloud, cybersecurity and digital services plus software products.
markets: Clients mainly in the US and Europe, with operations in about 60 countries.
rationale: IT services rivals sponsor F1; growing sports sponsorship and B2B hospitality with global enterprises.

name: Criteo
desc: Advertising technology company providing retargeting and retail media advertising for retailers, brands and agencies.
markets: Operates across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific with retail and brand clients.
rationale: B2B adtech brand with little consumer need; hospitality with retailers and agencies is the only angle.

name: Palo Alto Networks
desc: Cybersecurity company selling firewalls, cloud security and AI-driven security operations platforms to enterprises and governments.
markets: Over 70,000 organisations in more than 150 countries.
rationale: Cybersecurity rivals such as CrowdStrike and Zscaler sponsor F1; technology showcase and enterprise hospitality.
changed: Agreed to acquire CyberArk in 2025
